record crew health test.#comment: Test tracker bookkeeping for the crew health test. It opens and saves the Debug_Table file, so it runs in its own thread and never inside the damage path (the 169.12 stall happened right where every damage application opened that table).

start crew lifescore monitor.#comment: A second start in the same mission pass would double every impact (two monitors apply the damage twice), so it is refused and traced. L:CREW_MONITOR_STARTS counts the starts for the whole flight.

post crew safety message.#comment: Short crew status: the role instead of the member number and no score. The status always ends with a period.

params.status: Mission aborted, crew secured. Direct to hospital.

set_message.text: Crew emergency: personnel are deboarding for immediate hospital admission.

params.status: No hospital found. Returning to base.

set_message.text: Hoist operation failed. Land and wait for rescue support.

crew presence flags.#comment: Presence per person aboard. Pilot from L:IMPL_PILOT0 (0 = present). Copilot, medic and the rear crew come from the seat tracker, which follows every person between seats. SDK_CABIN_PAX_5: 0 no stretcher, 1 empty stretcher, 2 stretcher with patient.

monitor aircraft crash impact.#comment: Starts the impact model: initial state, velocity history and the loop. There is deliberately no watchdog that restarts the loop: a stalled thread must be explained, not hidden (the 169.12 stall is still under investigation). Stages are traced so that the last row shows where a thread stops.

crash monitor loop.#comment: One thread for the whole impact model, so there is no lock to leave stuck and no state shared between paths. Every tick (0.02 s) it reads the acceleration and the world velocity. Minor injuries: acceleration resultant of 80 ft/s2 (about 2.5 g), 0 to 3 (not below 70), plus 3 to 8 (not below 40) from 120 ft/s2; it rearms below 60. Crash tiers (rearm below 64): 150 ft/s2 or 25 ft/s lost gives 7 to 20 (not below 20); the loss of world velocity within about 0.2 s then gives 10 to 30 at 50 ft/s, 10 to 30 with failures and fires at 90 ft/s and 45 to 60 at 150 ft/s (ignores the member lock). The crash path has two more triggers that do not depend on catching an acceleration spike (a single-frame spike can fall between two ticks): a new simulator touchdown speed (PLANE TOUCHDOWN NORMAL VELOCITY changes and its square reaches 625) and a loss of 25 ft/s of world velocity within one tick below 100 ft above ground; either one grades the impact with the same squared-velocity table. Above 150 ft/s the crash is fatal for everyone aboard (score 100, ignores the member lock). While slew mode is active (IS SLEW ACTIVE, which also covers the repositioning done by the mission itself) and for 15 ticks after it, every trigger is suppressed, so a teleport is never taken for an impact; the height guard and the unchanged velocity during a pause are secondary. The damage chain is long, and the 169.16 test showed a RangeError (Maximum call stack size exceeded) at the catastrophic tier, after the three previous tiers had run in the same pass without a sleep: the stack of a thread only unwinds at a sleep, so every damage application (and every member inside it) is followed by a short sleep, and the catch starts with one so that its own trace cannot overflow. An error in a tick is caught and traced, and the loop goes on. Every impact traces probe_trigger and probe_after (L:CRASH, the simulator touchdown velocity, on-ground, height, vertical speed, ground speed, world vertical velocity before and now) to compare the signals in a test; a probe error is caught on its own and cannot stop the injuries.

then.#comment: A spike of acceleration alone is not an impact: a soft touchdown or a hoist jolt gives 120 to 170 ft/s2 for a frame with almost no change of velocity (169.20 test: 144 and 174 ft/s2 with 2 and 6 ft/s lost at 0.5 to 2.6 ft/s of descent). Without the touchdown or velocity trigger, the acceleration triggers count only when the velocity changed by at least 10 ft/s (dv2 100) in the window; otherwise the event is traced as ignored and both paths wait to be rearmed.

set_message.text: Impact detected. Crew shaken but conscious.
Severe impact detected. Crew injuries reported.
Heavy impact detected. Serious crew injuries likely.
Catastrophic impact detected. Crew casualties likely.

crew seat tracker tick.#comment: Who sits where. Persons keep their identity while moving between seats. A seat vacated and a seat filled in the same tick is a move; with several candidates the cabin-right seat takes the rear crew member first. A person leaving without a filled seat is outside; a filled seat without a mover takes the outside person by seat affinity (FO 3, P3 2, P1 4, P2 5).

crew member event announce.#comment: Announces a critical condition or a death to the survivors: dispatcher/RescueTrack message and on-screen message. The first event also announces the abort.

params.status: deceased. Mission aborted, proceed to hospital. Accident report required.

set_message.text: CREW LOSS: {0} deceased. Mission aborted, fly to the hospital.

params.status: critical. Mission aborted, all aboard. Accident report required.

set_message.text: CREW CRITICAL: {0}. Mission aborted, fly to the hospital.

then.#comment: Status 7 (unavailable for dispatch) only with automatic status reports (DISPATCHER_AUTO 0), through Update_raw from dispatchphase, which updates RescueTrack in the language of the active status table. Phases 5 and 6 are avoided: the NEW DISPATCH thread answers them with ready dispatch, which reopens the briefing page.

crew impact events.#comment: Evaluates every member marked after an impact once, with the final scores of the batch: alerts, critical and death events, survivors, the abort and the mission termination.

Pilot and copilot (or the only pilot when there is no copilot) are not fit to fly when dead or critical: a single pilot with one trained technical crew member can land only while the second one is fit, so both unfit ends the mission as with two deaths.
